To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of the low- lying eigenvalues of the Dirac operator is well approximated by the distribution of the smallest eigenvalue and that the distribution of this eigenvalue can be computed from the spectral density.

the spectral density of the Dirac operator at high temperature is well described by a universal function of the eigenvalue, that this function is independent of the gauge group and that it is well described by the random matrix model.

the distribution of the smallest eigenvalues of the lattice Dirac operator in QCD is well described by an ensemble of random matrices with the appropriate symmetries, and that there are no correlations between different regions in the low lying spectrum.
